# Research trail: geography topic discovery

Budget used: 8 searches. 11 fetch attempts, of which 5 were read; two of those were PDFs that the fetch tool returned as binary, so their saved copies were read through a local text extraction. The other 6 attempts read nothing, and nothing from them is used.

## Before searching
Ideas weighed without spending a search:
- Lake Natron's "stone" birds: the manual's own example, and a carcass picture the content rules forbid.
- Bir Tawil: much told already, and thin on physical geography.
- Europe's mild winters and the Gulf Stream argument: its decisive material would be a disputed climate claim.
- The Okavango Delta: usually told through its wildlife; the salt machinery is the untold part.
- The Casiquiare, and Saharan dust reaching the Amazon.

The last three were researched (T1, T2, T3).

## Searches
1. Okavango islands, salt, transpiration, McCarthy. Gave the transpiration-salt model; a UCT report of McCarthy's 2015 lecture (same scientist, snippet, not used); and the 2026 EGU abstract that challenges the model (read later as S2).
2. Casiquiare capture, GRL. Gave Stokes, Goldberg and Perron 2018 (S8, snippet), an AGU blog post (later a 404), and Pesquisa FAPESP (read later as S9): about a quarter of the water, up to 40,000 km2.
3. Saharan dust, Amazon, CALIPSO. Gave Yu et al. 2015's figures (S12) and the University of Maryland release (S13), both snippets.
4. Okavango flood timing and water balance. Gave the EGU 2011 abstract (read later as S3) and a 2023 study on the Angolan origin of the inflow (S7, snippet). Wikipedia's 96-98% and a tourism page's six-month lag were not used.
5. Termite mounds and the solute budget. Gave the Wits repository copy of McCarthy and Humphries 2024 (read as S1). Also a poster summary naming termite mounds and channel inversion as island origins (snippet, not in the ledger), and Dangerfield et al. 1998 on mound sizes (not used).
6. Ramberg and Wolski 2008. Gave a summary of its abstract (S5): 98-99% of the water lost to evapotranspiration, 94% of solutes retained, about 150,000 islands, 100,000-400,000 years. Never read.
7. NASA Earth Observatory on the Okavango. Gave the 2012 caption (read as S4). An ISS caption calling the lower margin "fault-bounded" and another page giving 2-5% outflow were snippets only and not used.
8. Humboldt, 1800, Casiquiare. Gave MDPI Water 2019 (S10) and the Geneva text on Buache (S11), both snippets. Encyclopedia.com was not used.

## Reads
- Read: S1 (the whole comment), S2 (the abstract, through the fetch tool's account with short quotes), S3 (the whole abstract), S4 (the whole caption), S9 (the whole article).
- Failed, nothing read:
  - Milzow et al. 2009's regional review on doc.rero.ch: HTTP 410.
  - Ramberg and Wolski on Springer: a redirect to an authorisation step, not followed.
  - UNESCO's World Heritage page: HTTP 403.
  - The Semantic Scholar record for Ramberg and Wolski: no abstract in it.
  - The AGU GeoSpace post: moved, then a 404.

## Dropped, and why
- The fault-bounded basin (R9 in "dropped"): only a search summary says it.
- The island count and ages (R10): a snippet only.
- NASA's "2 to 5 percent" outflow: a snippet; the read sources give under 1% and about 2%.
- For T2, a 1744 missionary's report of the Casiquiare (plain context at best, and T2 was not chosen), and a popular claim that cartographers still refuse to draw it.
- The delta's wildlife: predators and hunting are out under the content rules, and animals are not the subject. No shot shows an animal.

## Where I was unsure
- The decisive facts (almost no water leaves, the water is fresh, the salt is in the islands) each rest on two read sources from different teams. The mechanism, though (C08, C09: trees pull the water in, the brine sinks), rests on S1 alone. S1 cites independent tests that I did not read (Bauer et al. 2006; Bauer-Gottwein et al. 2007), so those claims stay "likely".
- S1 and S2 are on opposite sides of the same dispute. S2 is an unreviewed abstract, seen through the fetch tool's summary, and Jolivet et al. 2023 is known only indirectly. The film gives both sides and picks no winner.
- The per-year unit of S1's 380,000-tonne figure is implied by context, not stated.
- The outflow figure depends on how it is measured (under 1% at the southern outlet, about 2% as surface flow), so the script says "one or two percent".
- T2 and T3 rest mostly on search summaries. The comparison turns on how much each one's material can carry, not on verified details, and their snippet-only items carry a note saying so.
- Format: in the plan sketch, depends_on is written inside significance (as the brief asks) and on the beat too (where manual 07's beat map and the studio's check read it).

## Next reads, before any script
- Ramberg and Wolski 2008.
- Bauer et al. 2006 (the imaged brine plume).
- A source for the fault-bounded basin.
- Jolivet et al. 2023, in its own words.
- McCarthy 2006 (Journal of Hydrology), for the solute budget in its original form.
